pages.title: Architecture and Command Dispatcher
pages.purpose: Overview of the CLI's architecture: entrypoint, urfave/cli app construction, static command registration, flag and error handling, and support packages.
instructions: Describe cmd/step/main.go as the binary entrypoint that calls internal/cmd.Run.
Describe exec/exec.go wrappers over system exec, signal forwarding, and browser opening.
Describe flags/flags.go as the shared flag catalog and the utils package helpers for reading files and key details.
Explain how internal/cmd/root.go builds the urfave/cli app, registers commands via cli-utils/command.Retrieve, sets up writers, panic handler, STEPDEBUG behavior, and the config file flag.
Explain inject.go's InjectContext/wrap middleware pattern used to pass context into command actions.
Explain static command registration: packages call command.Register in init(), and cmd/step imports the command packages blank so their init runs.
Explain the plugin dispatch path in the app.Action fallback.

pages.title: Certificate Authority Integration
pages.purpose: How step interacts with step-ca: clients, token flows, provisioner prompts, bootstrap, ACME, offline mode, and admin management.
instructions: Describe the one-time token OTT generation in `step ca token` and the certificate/renew/revoke lifecycle.
Explain ACME flows: standalone/http and webroot challenge servers, ACMECreateCertFlow and ACMESignCSRFlow.
Explain admin management via AdminClient and provisioner add/update/remove commands.
Explain bootstrap: downloading/validating the root by fingerprint, writing $STEPPATH defaults.json and root_ca.crt, optional truststore install and contexts, and team-authority bootstrapping.
Explain offline mode: OfflineTokenFlow and NewOfflineCA load ca.json created by `step ca init` and sign without contacting the server.
Explain the CaClient interface and NewClient which returns an online ca.Client or an offline OfflineCA.

Explain the token flow: parseAudience builds the /1.0/* audience from ca-url, provisionerPrompt selects a provisioner, and NewTokenFlow dispatches by provisioner type (JWK, OIDC, X5C, K8sSA, cloud identity, SSHPOP, Nebula, ACME/SCEP errors).

pages.title: Certificate Command Group
pages.purpose: Standalone X.509 certificate operations independent of a CA: create, sign, inspect, lint, bundle, verify, install.
instructions: Describe the certificate command group and its profiles (leaf, self-signed, intermediate-ca, root-ca, csr).
Explain default validity durations and the template mechanism for customizing certificates.
Explain internal/cryptoutil KMS detection, attestor interface, and the internal/crlutil CRL helpers.
Explain the packaging/p12/pkcs12 operations.

pages.title: Change Guide: Add a New Command
pages.purpose: Focused maintenance guide walking through adding a new urfave/cli command to step.
instructions: Cover how to add to the app.Commands via cli-utils command.Retrieve and how to make it available.
Explain how to reuse shared flags from the flags package and errs/usage helpers for errors and docs.
Explain where to place the new command package, how to define and register the cli.Command with command.Register, and how cmd/step imports it so init() runs.
Follow the documented package-layout and registration steps.

pages.title: Change Guide: Modify the CA Token Flow
pages.purpose: Focused maintenance guide for extending the CA token-generation and certificate-provisioning flows when adding a new provisioner type or flow behavior.
instructions: Explain how the token signing dispatch maps each provisioner type to token generation methods, and how ACME/SCEP return errors.
Explain the flowContext/sharedContext and Option pattern for sharing state across commands.
Explain where new provisioner types fit in the token_flow dispatch and provisionerPrompt filters.

pages.title: Crypto Command Group
pages.purpose: The general-purpose crypto toolkit: subcommands, key derivation functions, security gating, and the underlying libraries.
instructions: Describe the crypto command group's purpose: balanced completeness and safety, gating insecure/subtle primitives with flags.
Document subcommand groups: jwk, jwt, jws, jwe, jose, hash, kdf, key, nacl, otp, rand, winpe.
Document the KDF package supporting scrypt, bcrypt, argon2i, argon2id and constant-time compare.
Explain keypair defaults (EC P-256, RSA 2048) from utils.GetKeyDetailsFromCLI.

pages.title: OAuth Device and Authorization Flows
pages.purpose: The step oauth command implementing OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authorisation, including the preconfigured Google client and device-grant flow.
instructions: Describe output modes: bare/header/oidc tokens.
Describe the preconfigured Google client IDs/device parameters and the ability to override with custom endpoints.
Explain the oauth command's flows: authorization code for installed apps, OOB, JWT bearer, refresh token, and device flow.

pages.title: SSH Integration
pages.purpose: How step generates, manages, and renews SSH user and host certificates, and interacts with the SSH agent.
instructions: Explain internal/sshutil key parsing (parseRSA/parseECDSA/parseED25519/parseDSA) and cert signer creation.
Explain the SSH agent integration: DialAgent, HasKeys, AddCertificate lifetimes, filter/expiry removal.
Explain the login flow including client-auth retry through OIDC identity tokens when the CA requires it.
Explain the ssh command group's subcommands (certificate, login, logout, config, hosts, inspect, list, proxycommand, renew, rekey, revoke, needsRenewal).
Mention systemd timer/service units for automated renewal.

pages.title: Testing and Integration Tests
pages.purpose: How the repository is tested: unit tests, the integration testscript suite, and the CI/build pipeline.
instructions: Describe CI workflows (ci.yml, actionci.yml) and the GoReleaser release configuration.
Describe the unit test layout co-located with sources.
Explain the Makefile targets: test, race, lint, govulncheck, build, goreleaser, install and bundle cross-compilation targets.
Explain the integration package using go-internal testscript with txtar testdata files.

pages.title: Token and Claim Construction
pages.purpose: Details the step-cli token package: default claims, signers, and the claim schemas used for one-time tokens.
instructions: Explain GenerateKeyID thumbprinting and the provision package.
Explain the claim name constants (sha, sans, step, user, cnf).
Explain the token.Token interface, Claims types, default claims (issuer, audience, validity windows), and the Sign method that sets kid and type JWT.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical onboarding: build, install, and run the step CLI; point to command groups and change guides.
instructions: Describe the default behavior of a bare `step`/`step help` invocation and how commands are registered.
Explain how to build and install the step binary (make build/install, go build).
Point to the architecture, ca integration, ssh integration, and crypto pages for more depth.
Summarize the major command groups (certificate, ca, crypto, ssh, oauth) with one-line purposes.
